issues.description: Constructor parameter type mismatch for class Bitmap24 in the template repository: Bitmap24 is declared in the template header with parameters of type long (Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height)) but implemented in the template source as Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository uses int for the constructor signature. This mismatch in the template (declaration vs. definition) will cause compilation/linkage errors or confusing compiler diagnostics for students and prevents them from building/running the provided example program without fixing the types.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor declaration and definition use the same parameter types. Prefer changing the template header to match the implementation and the solution: declare the constructor as Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) in template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp so it matches Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int, int) in the .cpp (and the solution). This keeps the template consistent with the solution and avoids build errors for students.

issues.description: Constructor signature for class Bitmap24 is inconsistent between the header and the implementation in the template repository and does not match the solution header. In the template header the constructor is declared as Bitmap24(long i_width, long i_height) (parameter names use the i_ prefix and type long), while the implementation (Bitmap24.cpp) defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (parameter names use p_ prefix and type int). The solution header uses Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). This mismatch (different parameter names and — more importantly — different parameter types) creates confusion for students about the intended constructor signature and may cause compilation or linkage issues or require students to resolve which signature to follow.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor declaration and definition use the same parameter types and (optionally) the same parameter names. Prefer the signature used in the solution for consistency: change the template header declaration to `Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height);` (or change the implementation to use `long`) and use consistent parameter names (e.g. `i_width`, `i_height`) in both declaration and definition so students have a single, unambiguous target to implement against.
